topic: UI theory-backed desktop app design foundation refactor
stack_version_constraints: Do not replace the existing Next/React renderer architecture.
Keep the Tauri runtime untouched for a CSS/UI foundation slice.
issue_discussion_notes: No high-signal issue thread was needed for this CSS foundation slice; the change was governed by established design systems and local regression tests.
community_signal_notes: Design-system convergence across Apple, Material, Fluent, Carbon, NN/g, and WCAG was used as evidence direction, not as direct proof of local fit.
selected_language: CSS custom properties with one React marker
language_decision_notes: CSS tokens solve the visual hierarchy problem with lower blast radius. React restructuring would risk state behavior, and Rust is not the right layer for surface styling.
architecture_decision_notes: Selected global token slice because it improves repeated surfaces immediately and gives tests a stable contract without freezing future screen-level redesign.
architecture_tradeoff_notes: Theory sources guide grouping, feedback, and accessibility; practitioner systems guide tokenization and density. Local browser validation remains the acceptance gate.
code_reference_notes: Existing CSS already uses design tokens and static tests, so the refactor extends that pattern instead of introducing a new styling framework.
folder_structure_options: Keep CSS/test changes inside workspace-monitor and platform checks
folder_structure_decision_notes: Kept changes in current renderer CSS and tests because the project has no separate design-system package yet and the user asked for implementation momentum.
folder_semantics_notes: Requirements and specs live in platform-desktop-app because this is a project-specific desktop UI change.
maintainability_notes: Static tests and readiness tokens preserve the foundation contract until a future shared design-system extraction is justified.
